A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCGA research work. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–E, including equations, tables, and rendered figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original attack-transfer experiments, component ablations, semantic analyses, and random-seed trials, including Tables 2–5 and supplementary Table S13.

after.justification: v6 retains original empirical results and adds targeted-attack experiments, additional defense evaluations, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The EMA teacher, early-block feature-consistency loss, adversarial objective, projection, and teacher-based inference remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. The targeted-attack integrations and plain-teacher ablations do not introduce a revised SCGA procedure.

E1.justification: v6 adds targeted ImageNet classification attacks requiring specified target labels, beyond v5's untargeted evaluations. It also adds DiffPure and rotation, smoothing, total-variation, and pixel-deflection test conditions. Existing datasets, dense-prediction tasks, and multimodal evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: CGNC and M3D are newly evaluated with and without SCGA in v6 Tables S12–S13. Table S15 also extends the adversarial-training/JPEG/BDR/R&P comparison from BIA in v5 Table 4 to include GAMA, FACL, and PDCL. The original main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New targeted protocols use one training epoch, VGG-family surrogates, an epsilon of 16/255, target success rate, and specified sets of eight or ten target classes. DiffPure introduces a 1,000-image evaluation at epsilon 10/255 and t=150. These are added protocols; the retained main experiments' settings and default hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds plain student-copy teachers with and without consistency loss. New Table 7 tests consistency weights, EMA coefficients, and individual versus joint early-block anchoring. Additional defense tests and Figure S10's t-SNE and frequency-band reconstructions substantially extend the robustness and mechanism analyses.

E5.justification: v6 newly reports compute averages over 10,000 training steps in Table S7; v5's compute reporting describes averaging over 1,000 iterations. The attack experiments retain the same three random trials and mean ± standard deviation reporting, moved from Table S13 to S20. No increase in attack-training seeds or new significance testing is established.

E6.justification: v6 adds substantial targeted-attack, defense, sensitivity, and compute results. For example, its new CGNC comparison reports average TSR of 4.84% without SCGA and 18.18% with SCGA; DiffPure results are mixed. Figure S5 also revises segmentation mIoU at tau=0.6 from 23.20 to 23.40. Main benchmark Tables 2–4 retain their values.

T1.justification: The loss equations, ACR and other metric definitions, feature-difference expression, and Appendix D Fourier-energy formulas are retained. Expanded spectral explanations and new empirical visualizations do not introduce a substantive mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: generator-internal semantic consistency, improved transfer without additional inference cost, and ACR as a complementary evaluation metric. New experiments support these existing claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v6 expands explanations of baseline-dependent CNN/ViT behavior, hyperparameter tradeoffs, and spectral redistribution, and identifies the DiffPure evaluation as preliminary and nonadaptive. Section E.6 removes explicit weak-semantic/U-Net and limited-task-coverage qualifications, although related caveats remain elsewhere in the appendices.

D1.justification: v5's promise of a future code release becomes repository/project access links in v6. New Tables S6–S7 disclose training batch size 48, total training time, peak memory, and forward/backward compute breakdowns. Frequency-reconstruction details are also added, while the original implementation settings remain largely intact.

R1.justification: v6 adds targeted-attack literature, including CGNC and M3D, and discusses dSVA's self-supervised ViT surrogate approach. Additional defense and t-SNE citations support the new analyses. The central positioning around generator-internal rather than surrogate-level regularization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most existing prose are retained. Changes include expanded explanatory passages, clearer baseline names, some corrected cross-references, updated affiliations and publication headers, acknowledgments, and a shortened conclusion and limitations discussion.

P2.justification: v6 substantially expands the displays with sensitivity, compute, targeted-attack, and defense tables, additional Table 5 columns, and new Figures S10–S11. Existing material is also reformatted: the perceptual-quality display changes from Figure S6 to Table S11, and Figure S5's legend identifies the metrics explicitly. Relocated figures are retained content.

improvement.justification: The added teacher controls and sensitivity studies better support SCGA's design choices, while targeted-attack and defense evaluations strengthen evidence about applicability. Code access information and fuller compute reporting improve reproducibility documentation. These gains are moderated by compute prose that still quotes the old measurements and fewer explicit limitations in E.6. Overall, v6 strengthens an already extensive empirical paper without resolving all reporting weaknesses.
